items.stem: In 472, what is the value of the digit 4?
items.hint: Look at which place the digit 4 is in: hundreds, tens or ones.
items.explanation: The digit 4 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 400.

items.stem: In 835, what is the value of the digit 3?
items.hint: Count the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds.
items.explanation: The digit 3 is in the tens place, so its value is 30.

items.stem: A number has 6 hundreds, 0 tens and 9 ones. What is the number?
items.hint: Write the hundreds digit first, then the tens, then the ones.
items.explanation: 6 hundreds, 0 tens and 9 ones make 609.

items.stem: Which number is "four hundred and six"?
items.hint: Count the hundreds, tens and ones in the words.
items.explanation: Four hundred and six has 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones: 406.

items.stem: Which number is "seven hundred and ninety"?
items.hint: There is no word for ones, so the ones digit is 0.
items.explanation: Seven hundred and ninety is 790.

items.stem: A shop sold six hundred and fifteen pencils. How is this number written?
items.hint: Six hundred, then fifteen.
items.explanation: Six hundred and fifteen is 615.

items.stem: Which number is the greatest?
items.hint: Compare the hundreds digits first.
items.explanation: 583 has the most hundreds and the most tens among numbers starting with 5.

items.stem: Which number is the smallest?
items.hint: Compare hundreds first, then tens.
items.explanation: 307 has 3 hundreds and 0 tens, so it is the smallest.

items.stem: Ali has 456 stickers, Ben has 465 and Chen has 446. Who has the most stickers?
items.hint: All have 4 hundreds. Compare the tens.
items.explanation: 465 has 6 tens, more than 456 and 446, so Ben has the most.

items.stem: What is the missing number? 240, 250, 260, ___, 280
items.hint: How much is added each time?
items.explanation: The numbers go up by 10, so the missing number is 270.

items.stem: What is the missing number? 900, 800, 700, ___, 500
items.hint: Are the numbers getting bigger or smaller?
items.explanation: The numbers go down by 100, so the missing number is 600.

items.stem: Mei counts in fives: 345, 350, 355, ___. What number does she say next?
items.hint: Add 5 to the last number.

items.stem: What is 100 more than 562?
items.hint: Only the hundreds digit changes.

items.stem: What is 10 less than 408?
items.hint: Take away one ten. There are no tens, so regroup a hundred.

items.stem: A box has 750 beads. Another box has 100 fewer beads. How many beads are in the other box?
items.hint: "Fewer" means take away.
Add the ones first, then the tens, then the hundreds. Remember to regroup.
Add the ones first, then the tens, then the hundreds. Remember to regroup.

items.stem: A library has 286 storybooks and 345 comics. How many books are there altogether?
items.hint: Add the ones first, then the tens, then the hundreds. Remember to regroup.
Subtract the ones first. If there are not enough ones or tens, regroup.
Subtract the ones first. If there are not enough ones or tens, regroup.

items.stem: There were 615 people at a concert. 247 people left early. How many people stayed?
items.hint: Subtract the ones first. If there are not enough ones or tens, regroup.
Subtract the ones first. If there are not enough ones or tens, regroup.
Subtract the ones first. If there are not enough ones or tens, regroup.

items.stem: Sam had $500. He spent $128 on a bicycle. How much money did he have left?
items.hint: Subtract the ones first. If there are not enough ones or tens, regroup.

items.stem: ___ + 245 = 600. What is the missing number?
items.hint: Find the number that is added to 245 to make 600. Use subtraction.

items.stem: 720 - ___ = 380. What is the missing number?
items.hint: The missing number is the part taken away. Subtract 380 from 720.

items.stem: Lina had some stamps. After she was given 165 more, she had 430 stamps. How many stamps did she have at first?
items.hint: Work backwards: take away the stamps she was given.

items.stem: A baker made 350 buns. He sold 128 in the morning and 95 in the afternoon. How many buns were left?
items.hint: Find how many were sold altogether first.

items.stem: Raju has 240 marbles. Gopal has 85 more than Raju. How many marbles do they have altogether?
items.hint: Find how many Gopal has first.
items.explanation: Gopal has 240 + 85 = 325. Altogether 240 + 325 = 565.

items.stem: A tank had 500 fish. 145 fish were moved out and 60 fish were put in. How many fish are in the tank now?
items.hint: Take away the fish moved out, then add the fish put in.

items.stem: Ahmad has 432 cards. Wei has 278 cards. How many more cards does Ahmad have than Wei?
items.hint: "How many more" means find the difference.

items.stem: A red ribbon is 365 cm long. A blue ribbon is 129 cm shorter. How long is the blue ribbon?
items.hint: "Shorter" means the blue ribbon is less.

items.stem: Farm A has 518 hens. Farm B has 87 fewer hens than Farm A. How many hens does Farm B have?
items.hint: "Fewer" tells you to subtract.
Count in 2s, 7 times.
Count in 2s, 9 times.

items.stem: Each child has 2 hands. How many hands do 8 children have?
items.hint: Count in 2s, 8 times.
Count in 5s, 6 times.
Count in 5s, 9 times.

items.stem: Each box holds 5 eggs. How many eggs are in 7 boxes?
items.hint: Count in 5s, 7 times.
Count in 10s, 4 times.
Count in 10s, 8 times.

items.stem: A pack has 10 crayons. How many crayons are in 6 packs?
items.hint: Count in 10s, 6 times.
Count in 3s, 7 times.
Count in 3s, 8 times.

items.stem: A tricycle has 3 wheels. How many wheels do 9 tricycles have?
items.hint: Count in 3s, 9 times.
Count in 4s, 6 times.
Count in 4s, 9 times.

items.stem: A table has 4 legs. How many legs do 7 tables have?
items.hint: Count in 4s, 7 times.

items.stem: Which is the same as 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4?
items.hint: Count how many 4s are added.
items.explanation: There are five 4s, so it is 5 × 4.

items.stem: Which is the same as 3 groups of 6?
items.hint: Groups of the same number can be written as multiplication.
items.explanation: 3 groups of 6 is 3 × 6 = 18.

items.stem: There are 6 plates with 5 strawberries on each plate. Which number sentence shows the total?
items.hint: Equal groups: number of groups × number in each group.
items.explanation: 6 groups of 5 is 6 × 5 = 30.

items.hint: Think: how many groups of 5 make 20?
Think: how many groups of 4 make 24?

items.stem: 18 sweets are shared equally among 3 children. How many sweets does each child get?
items.hint: Share equally or make equal groups. Use a times table.
Think: how many groups of 10 make 30?
Think: how many groups of 2 make 16?

items.stem: Mr Tan puts 35 chairs into rows of 5. How many rows are there?
items.hint: Share equally or make equal groups. Use a times table.

items.stem: Each pencil costs $3. How much do 8 pencils cost?
items.hint: Equal amounts: multiply.

items.stem: 28 children form groups of 4. How many groups are there?
items.hint: How many 4s make 28?

items.stem: A ribbon 40 cm long is cut into 5 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.hint: Cut into equal pieces: divide.

items.stem: Which unit should we use to measure the length of a classroom?
items.hint: A classroom is long. Choose the bigger unit of length.
items.explanation: Long lengths such as a classroom are measured in metres.

items.stem: Which unit should we use to measure the length of an eraser?
items.hint: An eraser is short.
items.explanation: Short lengths such as an eraser are measured in centimetres.

items.stem: Jun wants to find the length of his pencil case. Which is the most sensible answer?
items.hint: Think about how big a pencil case is.
items.explanation: A pencil case is about 20 cm long.

items.stem: Look at the ruler. How long is the pencil?
items.hint: Find the mark where the pencil starts and the mark where it ends.
items.explanation: The pencil starts at 0 cm and ends at 13 cm, so it is 13 cm long.

items.stem: Look at the ruler. How long is the crayon?
items.hint: The crayon does not start at 0. Count the centimetres from its left end to its right end.
items.explanation: The crayon goes from the 2 cm mark to the 9 cm mark. 9 − 2 = 7, so it is 7 cm long.

items.stem: Look at the ruler. How long is the ribbon?
items.hint: Where does the ribbon start? Where does it end? Find the difference.
items.explanation: The ribbon goes from the 5 cm mark to the 16 cm mark. 16 − 5 = 11, so it is 11 cm long.

items.stem: Rope A is 3 m long. Rope B is 5 m long. Rope C is 2 m long. Which rope is the longest?
items.hint: Compare the numbers of metres.
items.explanation: 5 m is the greatest length, so Rope B is the longest.

items.stem: Rod P is 45 cm, Rod Q is 54 cm and Rod R is 40 cm. Which rod is the shortest?
items.hint: Find the smallest length.
items.explanation: 40 cm is the shortest length.

items.stem: A scarf is 85 cm long. A belt is 58 cm long. How much longer is the scarf than the belt?
items.hint: Find the difference.
items.explanation: 85 cm - 58 cm = 27 cm.

items.stem: Siti walked 125 m to the park and then 68 m to the library. How far did she walk altogether?
items.hint: Altogether means add.

items.stem: A ribbon was 90 cm long. Mum cut off 35 cm. How long is the ribbon now?
items.hint: Cut off means take away.
items.explanation: 90 cm - 35 cm = 55 cm.

items.stem: A fence has 4 parts. Each part is 5 m long. How long is the fence?
items.hint: Equal parts: multiply.

items.stem: Which unit should we use to find the mass of a watermelon?
items.hint: A watermelon is heavy.
items.explanation: Heavy things are measured in kilograms.

items.stem: Which unit should we use to find the mass of a paper clip?
items.hint: A paper clip is very light.
items.explanation: Light things are measured in grams.

items.stem: Which is the most sensible mass of a school bag with books inside?
items.hint: Think about whether you can carry it easily.
items.explanation: A school bag with books has a mass of about 3 kg.

items.stem: The scale shows the mass of a bag of flour. What is its mass?
items.hint: Each big mark is 100 g. What is each small mark worth?
items.explanation: The pointer is halfway between 400 g and 500 g, on the small mark. Each small mark is 50 g, so the mass is 450 g.

items.stem: The scale shows the mass of a pumpkin. What is its mass?
items.hint: Only every second mark has a number. What is each unmarked step worth?
items.explanation: The numbers go up in 2s, so each mark is 1 kg. The pointer is one mark after 6 kg, so the mass is 7 kg.

items.stem: The scale shows the mass of some grapes. What is their mass?
items.hint: Count how many small steps make 100 g on this scale.
items.explanation: There are 5 steps between 200 g and 300 g, so each step is 20 g. The pointer is 3 steps after 200 g: 200 + 60 = 260 g.

items.stem: A box of books has a mass of 18 kg. The empty box has a mass of 3 kg. What is the mass of the books?
items.hint: Take away the mass of the box.
items.explanation: 18 kg - 3 kg = 15 kg.

items.stem: Each packet of flour has a mass of 2 kg. What is the mass of 6 packets?
items.hint: Equal masses: multiply.

items.stem: Ken has a mass of 28 kg. His brother is 9 kg heavier. What is his brother's mass?
items.hint: "Heavier" means more.
items.explanation: 28 kg + 9 kg = 37 kg.

items.stem: Which container is most likely to hold about 1 litre of water?
items.hint: One litre is a bottle of drink.
items.explanation: A large water bottle holds about 1 litre.

items.stem: Jug A holds 4 ℓ. Jug B holds 7 ℓ. Jug C holds 5 ℓ. Which jug holds the most?
items.hint: Compare the numbers of litres.
items.explanation: 7 ℓ is the most.

items.stem: A pail had 10 ℓ of water. Dad used 4 ℓ to wash the car. How much water was left?
items.hint: Used means take away.

items.stem: Bottle P holds 3 ℓ more than Bottle Q. Bottle Q holds 5 ℓ. How much does Bottle P hold?
items.hint: "More than" means add.

items.stem: A tank holds 20 ℓ. A pail holds 5 ℓ. How many pails of water are needed to fill the tank?
items.hint: How many 5s make 20?
items.explanation: 20 ℓ ÷ 5 ℓ = 4 pails.

items.stem: Mum pours 2 ℓ of soup into each of 4 pots. How much soup does she pour altogether?
items.hint: Equal amounts: multiply.

items.stem: What time does the clock show?
items.hint: Count the minutes past the hour in fives, then in ones.
items.explanation: The hour hand is just past 4. The minute hand is 2 small marks after 3 (15 minutes), so it is 17 minutes past 4: 4.17.

items.stem: What time is shown on this clock?
items.hint: The hour hand has not reached 8 yet. Which hour has passed?
items.explanation: The hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is 7. The minute hand is 3 small marks after 8 (40 minutes), so it is 7.43.

items.stem: Lunch starts at the time on this clock. What time does lunch start?
items.hint: The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes.
items.explanation: The hour hand is just past 12. The minute hand is 3 small marks after 7 (35 minutes), so it is 12.38.

items.stem: Mei wakes up at 6.30 in the morning. How do we write this time?
items.hint: Morning times use a.m.
items.explanation: Times from midnight to noon are a.m.: 6.30 a.m.

items.stem: Dinner is at 7 o'clock in the evening. How do we write this time?
items.hint: Times after noon use p.m.
items.explanation: Evening times are p.m.: 7.00 p.m.

items.stem: Which activity most likely happens at 10.00 p.m.?
items.hint: p.m. after 6 is night time.
items.explanation: 10.00 p.m. is at night, when most children are sleeping.

items.stem: A lesson starts at 9.00 a.m. and ends at 10.00 a.m. How long is the lesson?
items.hint: Count the hours from 9 to 10.
items.explanation: From 9.00 a.m. to 10.00 a.m. is 1 hour.

items.stem: A movie starts at 2.00 p.m. and lasts 2 hours. What time does it end?
items.hint: Count on 2 hours from 2.00 p.m.

items.stem: Ali started reading at 3.15 p.m. He read for 30 minutes. What time did he stop?
items.hint: Count on 30 minutes from 3.15.
items.explanation: 3.15 p.m. + 30 minutes = 3.45 p.m.

items.stem: 1 hour = ___ minutes
items.hint: Think of the minute hand going all the way round once.
items.explanation: There are 60 minutes in 1 hour.

items.stem: 1 hour 20 minutes = ___ minutes
items.hint: Change 1 hour to minutes first.
items.explanation: 60 + 20 = 80 minutes.

items.stem: A bus ride takes 90 minutes. How long is that in hours and minutes?
items.hint: 60 minutes make 1 hour. How many minutes are left?
items.explanation: 90 minutes = 60 minutes + 30 minutes = 1 h 30 min.

items.stem: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
items.hint: Count all the equal parts. Then count the shaded parts.
items.explanation: The circle has 4 equal parts and 1 is shaded, so 1/4 is shaded.

items.stem: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.hint: The bottom number is the number of equal parts in the whole.
items.explanation: The bar has 6 equal parts and 5 are shaded, so 5/6 is shaded.

items.stem: What fraction of the circle is NOT shaded?
items.hint: Count the parts that are white.
items.explanation: The circle has 8 equal parts. 3 are shaded, so 5 are not shaded: 5/8.

items.stem: Which fraction is the greatest?
items.hint: For unit fractions, fewer equal parts means bigger parts.
items.explanation: Halves are bigger than fifths, eighths or tenths, so 1/2 is greatest.

items.stem: Which fraction is the smallest?
items.hint: All are ninths. Compare the top numbers.
items.explanation: With the same number of equal parts, 2/9 is the smallest.

items.stem: Ali ate 1/3 of a cake. Ben ate 1/6 of the same-sized cake. Who ate more?
items.hint: Thirds are bigger pieces than sixths.
items.explanation: 1/3 is greater than 1/6, so Ali ate more.

items.stem: Arrange from smallest to greatest: 1/3, 1/12, 1/7
items.hint: The more equal parts, the smaller each part.
items.explanation: Twelfths are smallest and thirds are biggest: 1/12, 1/7, 1/3.

items.stem: Arrange from greatest to smallest: 3/10, 9/10, 6/10
items.hint: All are tenths. Compare the top numbers.
items.explanation: 9 tenths, then 6 tenths, then 3 tenths.

items.stem: Three friends drank 1/4, 1/2 and 1/5 of the same-sized bottles. Which amount is the smallest?
items.hint: Fifths are smaller than quarters and halves.
items.explanation: 1/5 is the smallest of these unit fractions.

items.hint: The fractions have the same bottom number. Add only the top numbers.
items.explanation: 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7. The bottom number stays the same.

items.hint: Add the top numbers; keep the bottom number.

items.stem: Siti ate 2/10 of a cake and her sister ate 5/10 of it. What fraction of the cake did they eat altogether?
items.hint: Altogether means add. The bottom numbers are the same.
Subtract only the top numbers.
items.explanation: 7/8 - 3/8 = 4/8. The bottom number stays the same.

items.hint: The bottom number does not change.

items.stem: A tank was 11/12 full. Water equal to 5/12 of the tank's full capacity was used. What fraction of the tank is full now?
items.hint: Both fractions describe parts of the same full tank. Subtract the amount used.
items.explanation: The full tank is the whole in both fractions: 11/12 - 5/12 = 6/12. The tank is now 6/12 full.

items.stem: Look at the picture graph. How many children chose swimming?
items.hint: Read the key first. How many children does one picture stand for?
items.explanation: Swimming has 4 stars and each star stands for 2 children. 4 × 2 = 8 children.

items.stem: Look at the picture graph. How many books were borrowed on Tuesday?
items.hint: Count the pictures for Tuesday, then use the key.
items.explanation: Tuesday has 5 circles and each circle stands for 5 books. 5 × 5 = 25 books.

items.stem: Look at the picture graph. How many more stickers does Mei have than Ali?
items.hint: Find the difference in pictures first, then use the key.
items.explanation: Mei has 6 triangles and Ali has 4: 2 more triangles. Each triangle stands for 10 stickers, so Mei has 20 more.

items.stem: How many apples are there in Basket A and Basket B altogether?
items.hint: Add the pictures for A and B, then use the key.
items.explanation: A has 5 squares and B has 2: 7 squares. Each square stands for 3 apples. 7 × 3 = 21 apples.

items.stem: Which colour was chosen by 8 more pupils than Green?
items.hint: Each picture stands for 4 pupils. How many more pictures make 8 more pupils?
items.explanation: 8 more pupils is 2 more pictures. Green has 2 circles, so look for 4 circles: Yellow.

items.stem: There are 12 red cars. How many pictures should be drawn in the Red row?
items.hint: Read the key. How many cars does one picture stand for?
items.explanation: Each picture stands for 2 cars. 12 ÷ 2 = 6 pictures.

items.stem: Which shape has exactly 4 sides?
items.hint: Count the straight sides of each shape.
items.explanation: Shape B is a rectangle with 4 sides. A has 3, C has 5 and D has 6.

items.stem: Which shape is a semicircle?
items.hint: A semicircle is half of a circle.
items.explanation: Shape B is half of a circle: a semicircle. A is a circle, C is a quarter circle and D is a square.

items.stem: Which shape is a quarter circle?
items.hint: A quarter circle has two straight sides that meet at a square corner, and one curved side.
items.explanation: Shape C is one quarter of a circle. A is a semicircle, B is a triangle and D is a circle.

items.stem: Which solid has 6 square faces?
items.hint: Look for a solid whose faces are all the same square.
items.explanation: Solid A is a cube: it has 6 square faces. B is a cylinder, C is a cone and D is a sphere.

items.stem: Which solid is a cone?
items.hint: A cone has one flat circle at the bottom and comes to a point.
items.explanation: Solid B is a cone. A is a cuboid, C is a sphere and D is a cylinder.

items.stem: A tin of soup has the same shape as one of these solids. Which one?
items.hint: A tin has two flat circle ends and a curved side.
items.explanation: Solid C is a cylinder, the same shape as a tin. A is a sphere, B is a cube and D is a cuboid.

items.stem: What comes next? ○ △ □ ○ △ □ ○ △ ___
items.hint: Find the group of shapes that repeats.
items.explanation: The pattern ○ △ □ repeats, so □ comes next.

items.stem: What comes next? big ○, small ○, big ○, small ○, ___
items.hint: Look at how the size changes.
items.explanation: Size changes big, small, big, small. Next is big ○.

items.stem: Beads are threaded red, red, blue, red, red, blue. What colour is the 9th bead?
items.hint: The pattern repeats every 3 beads.
items.explanation: Beads 3, 6 and 9 are blue.

items.stem: The square is cut along the dashed line. What two shapes are formed?
items.hint: Imagine cutting from one corner to the opposite corner.
items.explanation: The dashed line joins opposite corners, so each piece has 3 sides: 2 triangles.

items.stem: These two pieces are the same size. They are put together along their straight edges. What shape is formed?
items.hint: Each piece is half of a shape.
items.explanation: Each piece is a semicircle (half a circle). Two equal semicircles joined along their straight edges make a circle.

items.stem: Two equal squares are placed side by side. What shape is the whole figure?
items.hint: Look at the outline of the whole figure, not the line in the middle.
items.explanation: The outline has 4 straight sides and 4 square corners, with two long sides and two short sides: a rectangle.

items.stem: Sam has two $5 notes and three 50-cent coins. How much money does he have?
items.hint: Add the dollars and the cents separately.

items.stem: How much is one $10 note, one $2 note and four 20-cent coins?
items.hint: Count the notes, then the coins.

items.stem: Mei has 3 one-dollar coins and 5 ten-cent coins. How much does she have?
items.hint: Five 10-cent coins make 50 cents.

items.stem: How is "4 dollars and 25 cents" written?
items.hint: Dollars come before the dot; cents after.
items.explanation: 4 dollars and 25 cents is $4.25.

items.stem: How is "9 dollars and 5 cents" written?
items.hint: Cents always use two digits.
items.explanation: 5 cents is written 05, so $9.05.

items.stem: A toy costs $16.40. How much is that in dollars and cents?
items.hint: The digits after the dot are cents.
items.explanation: $16.40 is 16 dollars and 40 cents.

items.stem: A book costs $8 and a pen costs $3. How much do they cost altogether?
items.hint: Altogether means add.

items.stem: Ali had 90 cents. He bought a sweet for 45 cents. How much money did he have left?
items.hint: Take away what he spent.
items.explanation: 90 cents - 45 cents = 45 cents.

items.stem: Mum paid $20 for a toy that costs $13. How much change did she get?
items.hint: Change = money paid - cost.

items.stem: Which is equal to 4 × 5?
items.hint: Changing the order of the numbers in multiplication does not change the answer.
The same two numbers are multiplied in a different order.

items.stem: There are 2 rows of 5 chairs. Mei says there are also 5 rows of 2 chairs if she turns around. Which sentence shows this?
items.hint: Both ways count the same chairs.

items.stem: Which amount is the greatest?
items.hint: Compare the dollars first, then the cents.
items.explanation: $5.20 has 5 dollars and 20 cents, more than $5.02.

items.stem: Which amount is the smallest?
items.hint: All the dollars are the same except one. Then compare cents.
items.explanation: $1.09 has only 9 cents after the dollar.

items.stem: A pen costs $3.40 and a ruler costs $3.15. Which costs more?
items.hint: The dollars are the same. Compare the cents.
items.explanation: 40 cents is more than 15 cents, so the pen costs more.

items.stem: In which figure is exactly one half shaded?
items.hint: For a half, the whole must be cut into 2 EQUAL parts.
items.explanation: In A the bar is cut into 2 equal parts and 1 is shaded: one half. B has 2 parts that are not equal; C shows 1/3 and D shows 1/4.

items.stem: What fraction of the circle is shaded?
items.hint: Check that the parts are equal, then count them.
items.explanation: The circle has 3 equal parts and 1 is shaded, so 1/3 is shaded.

items.stem: A ribbon is folded into equal parts. The shaded part is cut off. What fraction of the ribbon is cut off?
items.hint: Count all the equal parts of the ribbon, including the shaded one.
items.explanation: The ribbon has 5 equal parts and 1 is cut off, so 1/5 of the ribbon is cut off.

items.stem: Which is the heaviest?
items.hint: Compare the numbers of kilograms.
items.explanation: 6 kg is the greatest mass.

items.stem: Arrange from lightest to heaviest: 300 g, 30 g, 130 g
items.hint: Find the smallest mass first.

items.stem: A box of crayons is 250 g and a box of pencils is 175 g. How much lighter is the box of pencils?
items.hint: "Lighter by" means find the difference.

items.stem: In 6385, what is the value of the digit 6?
items.hint: Which place is the 6 in?
items.explanation: The 6 is in the thousands place, so its value is 6000.

items.stem: In 4907, what is the value of the digit 9?
items.hint: Count the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds.
items.explanation: The 9 is in the hundreds place: 900.

items.stem: A number has 7 thousands, 0 hundreds, 3 tens and 8 ones. What is the number?
items.hint: Remember to write 0 for the hundreds.

items.stem: Which number is "five thousand and twelve"?
items.hint: Five thousand, no hundreds, then twelve.
items.explanation: Five thousand and twelve is 5012.

items.stem: Which number is "eight thousand, three hundred and sixty"?
items.hint: There is no word for ones.

items.stem: How is 9040 written in words?
items.hint: Read the thousands, then the tens.
items.explanation: 9040 is nine thousand and forty.

items.stem: Which number is the greatest?
items.hint: Compare thousands, then hundreds, then tens.
items.explanation: 7621 has the greatest hundreds and tens among those with 7 thousands.

items.stem: Arrange from smallest to greatest: 3480, 3408, 3840
items.hint: All have 3 thousands. Compare the hundreds.

items.stem: Three schools have 2856, 2865 and 2586 pupils. Which school has the fewest pupils?
items.hint: Compare hundreds first.
items.explanation: 2586 has 5 hundreds, fewer than 8 hundreds.

items.stem: What is the missing number? 4250, 4500, 4750, ___
items.hint: How much is added each time?
items.explanation: The numbers go up by 250. 4750 + 250 = 5000.

items.stem: What is the missing number? 9100, 8100, ___, 6100
items.hint: The numbers go down by the same amount.

items.stem: What is 1000 more than 8956?
items.hint: Only the thousands digit changes.

items.stem: Which number is odd?
items.hint: Look at the ones digit only.
items.explanation: A number ending in 7 is odd.

items.stem: Which number is even?
items.hint: Even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8.
items.explanation: 5794 ends in 4, so it is even.

items.stem: What is the greatest even number that can be made with the digits 3, 8, 1 and 6, each used once?
items.hint: An even number must end in an even digit. Put the biggest digits in front.
items.explanation: 8316 ends with 6 and uses the larger digits in front.

items.hint: Line up the places. Work from the ones and regroup where needed.
Line up the places. Work from the ones and regroup where needed.

items.stem: A school raised $6000 for charity. It has given $1847 so far. How much more does it have to give?
items.hint: Line up the places. Work from the ones and regroup where needed.

items.stem: A farm had 4560 chickens. 1275 were sold and 830 chicks hatched. How many chickens are there now?
items.hint: Subtract the chickens sold, then add the chicks.

items.stem: Pen A has 2400 ducks. Pen B has 650 more ducks than Pen A. How many ducks are there altogether?
items.hint: Find Pen B first.

items.stem: Mr Lim had $8500. He spent $2350 on a sofa and $1890 on a table. How much did he have left?
items.hint: Find the total spent first.

items.hint: Use the multiplication table of 6.

items.stem: There are 7 days in a week. How many days are there in 9 weeks?
items.hint: Use the multiplication table of 7.

items.hint: Use the multiplication table of 8.

items.hint: Use the multiplication table of 9.

items.stem: 48 children are put into teams of 6. How many teams are there?
items.hint: How many 6s make 48?
items.explanation: 48 ÷ 6 = 8 teams.

items.hint: Multiply the ones first, then the tens, then the hundreds. Add any regrouped numbers.
Multiply the ones first, then the tens, then the hundreds. Add any regrouped numbers.

items.stem: A bus can carry 64 passengers. How many passengers can 7 buses carry?
items.hint: Multiply the ones first, then the tens, then the hundreds. Add any regrouped numbers.

items.stem: Each carton has 245 ml of milk. How much milk is in 6 cartons, in ml?
items.hint: Multiply the ones first, then the tens, then the hundreds. Add any regrouped numbers.
Divide from the greatest place first.
Divide from the greatest place first.

items.stem: 945 stickers are shared equally among 5 classes. How many stickers does each class get?
items.hint: Divide from the greatest place first.
Find the biggest multiple of 5 that is not more than 47.
items.explanation: 5 × 9 = 45 and 47 - 45 = 2, so 9 remainder 2.

items.hint: The remainder must be smaller than 6.

items.stem: 50 pupils go on a trip. Each van holds 8 pupils. What is the least number of vans needed?
items.hint: 50 ÷ 8 leaves a remainder. The remaining pupils need a van too.
items.explanation: 50 ÷ 8 = 6 remainder 2. The 2 pupils need another van, so 7 vans.

items.stem: Mrs Tan bought 6 boxes of oranges. Each box had 24 oranges. She gave away 38 oranges. How many oranges did she have left?
items.hint: Find the total number of oranges first.

items.stem: A shop had 315 pens. It packed them equally into 9 boxes and sold 4 boxes. How many pens were sold?
items.hint: Find how many pens are in one box first.
items.explanation: 315 ÷ 9 = 35 pens per box. 4 × 35 = 140 pens.

items.stem: Ali saved $8 a week for 9 weeks. He then spent $25 on a game. How much did he have left?
items.hint: Find his total savings first.

items.stem: Ben has 3 times as many marbles as Ali. Ali has 45 marbles. How many marbles does Ben have?
items.hint: Draw 1 unit for Ali and 3 units for Ben.
items.explanation: Ben has 3 × 45 = 135 marbles.

items.stem: A ribbon is 4 times as long as a string. The ribbon is 92 cm long. How long is the string?
items.hint: The ribbon is 4 units. Find 1 unit.

items.stem: Mei has 5 times as many stamps as Siti. Together they have 240 stamps. How many stamps does Siti have?
items.hint: Together there are 1 + 5 = 6 units.
items.explanation: 240 ÷ 6 = 40 stamps for Siti.

items.hint: Add the cents and regroup 100 cents as $1.
Line up the decimal points.

items.stem: A shirt costs $18.50 and a cap costs $9.75. How much do they cost together?
items.hint: Add the two prices.
Regroup $1 as 100 cents.
There are not enough cents. Regroup.

items.stem: Ali paid $50 for a bag costing $36.70. How much change did he get?
items.hint: Change = amount paid - cost.

items.stem: Mum bought 3 kg of chicken at $6.50 per kg. How much did she pay?
items.hint: Multiply or add $6.50 three times.

items.stem: Siti had $40. She bought a book for $12.90 and a pen for $3.45. How much did she have left?
items.hint: Find the total spent first.

items.stem: A notebook costs $2.80. Jun has $10. How much more money does he need to buy 4 notebooks?
items.hint: Find the cost of 4 notebooks first.

items.stem: 3 m 45 cm = ___ cm
A rope is 506 cm long. What is its length in metres and centimetres?
items.hint: Each 100 cm is 1 m.
items.explanation: 506 cm = 500 cm + 6 cm = 5 m 6 cm.

items.hint: Each 1000 g is 1 kg.

items.stem: A bag of rice weighs 5 kg. 1 kg 400 g of rice is used. How much rice is left?
items.hint: Change 5 kg to 4 kg 1000 g.
Each 1000 ml is 1 ℓ.

items.stem: A jug holds 1 ℓ 200 ml of juice. Mum pours out 450 ml. How much juice is left?
items.hint: Change 1 ℓ 200 ml to millilitres first.

items.stem: A path is 1 km 250 m long. Ali has walked 680 m. How much further must he walk?
items.hint: Change 1 km 250 m to metres.

items.stem: Each bottle holds 350 ml of water. How much water do 4 bottles hold?
items.hint: Multiply, then change to litres and millilitres.

items.stem: A box with 6 identical tins has a mass of 2 kg 100 g. The empty box has a mass of 300 g. What is the mass of 1 tin?
items.hint: Find the mass of all the tins first.

items.stem: Which is the best estimate for the time taken to tie a shoelace?
items.hint: Think about how quickly you can do it.
items.explanation: Tying a shoelace takes about 10 seconds.

items.stem: 1 minute = ___ seconds
items.hint: Think of the second hand going round once.
items.explanation: There are 60 seconds in 1 minute.

items.stem: Ali ran 100 m in 18 seconds. Ben took 4 seconds longer. How long did Ben take?
items.hint: "Longer" means more time.
items.explanation: 18 + 4 = 22 seconds.

items.stem: A show starts at 2.40 p.m. and ends at 4.15 p.m. How long is the show?
items.hint: Count on to the next hour, then to the end time.

items.stem: A lesson starts at 10.50 a.m. and lasts 45 minutes. What time does it end?
items.hint: Count 10 minutes to 11.00, then the rest.

items.stem: A train journey ended at 1.20 p.m. It took 2 h 30 min. What time did it start?
items.hint: Count backwards from the end time.

items.stem: 2 h 15 min = ___ min
items.hint: 1 h = 60 min.
items.explanation: 120 min + 15 min = 135 min.

items.stem: 200 min = ___ h ___ min
items.hint: How many groups of 60 are in 200?

items.stem: Mei practised piano for 95 minutes. How long is that in hours and minutes?
items.hint: Take away 60 minutes for 1 hour.

items.stem: Which fraction is equivalent to 1/2?
items.hint: Multiply the top and bottom by the same number.

items.stem: Which fraction is equivalent to 2/3?
items.hint: What do you multiply 3 by to get 12?
items.explanation: 2/3 = 8/12 (multiply top and bottom by 4).

items.stem: Ali ate 4/8 of a pie. Which fraction shows the same amount in simplest form?
items.hint: Divide the top and bottom by the same number.
items.explanation: 4/8 = 1/2 (divide top and bottom by 4).

items.stem: Which is greater, 3/4 or 5/8?
items.hint: Change 3/4 into eighths.
items.explanation: 3/4 = 6/8, which is greater than 5/8.

items.stem: Which fraction is the smallest: 1/2, 2/5, 7/10?
items.hint: Change them all into tenths.

items.stem: Siti walked 2/3 km and Mei walked 5/6 km. Who walked further?
items.hint: Change 2/3 into sixths.
items.explanation: 2/3 = 4/6, which is less than 5/6, so Mei walked further.

items.hint: Change 1/4 into eighths first.
Change 1/3 into sixths.

items.stem: Ali painted 1/5 of a wall and Ben painted 3/10 of it. What fraction of the wall did they paint?
items.hint: Change 1/5 into tenths.
Change 1/3 into sixths.
1 whole = 8/8.

items.stem: A ribbon was 9/10 m long. Mei used 2/5 m of it. How much ribbon was left?
items.hint: Change 2/5 into tenths.

items.stem: What is the area of the shaded figure?
items.hint: Count the 1-cm squares. Area is measured in square centimetres.
items.explanation: The figure covers 12 squares of 1 cm by 1 cm, so its area is 12 cm².

items.stem: Find the area of the shaded figure.
items.hint: Count the squares row by row.
items.explanation: There are 3 rows of 5 squares. 3 × 5 = 15 squares, so the area is 15 cm².

items.stem: Some squares in this figure are only half shaded. What is the area of the shaded figure?
items.hint: Two half squares make one whole square.
items.explanation: There are 9 whole squares and 2 half squares. 2 halves make 1 whole, so the area is 9 + 1 = 10 cm².

items.stem: A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. What is its area?
items.hint: Area of a rectangle = length × breadth.

items.stem: A square has sides of 7 m. What is its area?
items.hint: Area of a square = side × side.

items.stem: A rectangular garden has an area of 36 m². It is 9 m long. How wide is it?
items.hint: Length × breadth = area. Which number times 9 gives 36?

items.stem: A rectangle is 9 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
items.hint: Perimeter is the distance all round: add all four sides.

items.stem: A square has sides of 6 cm. What is its perimeter?
items.hint: A square has 4 equal sides.

items.stem: A square field has a perimeter of 48 m. What is the length of one side?
items.hint: The 4 sides are equal.

items.stem: Rectangle A is 6 cm by 2 cm. Rectangle B is 4 cm by 3 cm. Which statement is true?

options.text: B has a bigger perimeter than A.

items.hint: Work out both areas and both perimeters.
items.explanation: Both areas are 12 cm². Perimeters are 16 cm and 14 cm.

items.stem: A fence goes all round a garden. Which measurement tells the length of the fence?
items.hint: The fence goes around the edge.
items.explanation: The distance around the edge is the perimeter.

items.stem: Mum wants to cover a table top with cloth. Which measurement does she need?
items.hint: The cloth covers the whole surface.
items.explanation: Covering a surface needs its area.

items.stem: Which angle is a right angle?
items.hint: Check each angle with the corner of a square piece of paper.
items.explanation: Angle B fits the square corner exactly, so it is a right angle. A and D are smaller; C is larger.

items.stem: How many right angles are inside this figure?
items.hint: Check each corner inside the figure with a square corner.
items.explanation: The two corners on the right are right angles. The top-left corner is larger and the bottom-left corner is smaller than a right angle.

items.stem: At which time do the hands of the clock make a right angle?
items.hint: A right angle is a quarter turn.
items.explanation: At 3.00 (clock A) the hands are a quarter turn apart: a right angle. At 1.00 and 10.00 the angle is smaller; at 6.00 the hands form a straight line.

items.stem: Which angle is smaller than a right angle?
items.hint: A smaller angle has arms that are closer together than a square corner.
items.explanation: Angle A is less than a quarter turn. B is a right angle; C and D are greater than a right angle.

items.stem: Compare this angle with a right angle.

options.text: It is smaller than a right angle.
It is greater than a right angle.

items.hint: Imagine placing a square corner on the angle.
items.explanation: The arms open wider than a square corner, so the angle is greater than a right angle.

items.stem: Which angle is the largest?
items.hint: The size of an angle is how far the arms open, not how long they are.
items.explanation: The arms of angle D open the widest, so D is the largest angle.

items.stem: How many angles does this figure have?
items.hint: An angle is made where two straight sides meet. Count the corners.
items.explanation: The figure has 3 corners where sides meet, so it has 3 angles.

items.stem: How many angles are there in this figure?
items.hint: Count each corner once as you go around the figure.
items.explanation: The figure has 5 straight sides and 5 corners, so it has 5 angles.

items.stem: A square and a triangle are joined to make this figure. How many angles does the outline have?
items.hint: Count only the corners on the outside of the figure.
items.explanation: Going around the outline there are 5 corners: 1 at the top and 4 more below it. So the outline has 5 angles.

items.stem: Which pair of lines is perpendicular?
items.hint: Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle.
items.explanation: The lines in B meet at a right angle, so they are perpendicular. A are parallel; C and D meet at angles that are not right angles.

items.stem: ABCD is a rectangle. Which sides are perpendicular to side AB?
items.hint: Look for sides that meet AB at a right angle.
items.explanation: AD and BC each meet AB at a right-angled corner, so both are perpendicular to AB. DC is parallel to AB.

items.stem: Which letter is made only of lines that are perpendicular to each other?
items.hint: Check each place where two lines of the letter meet.
items.explanation: The two lines of the letter in A meet at a right angle. The other letters have lines that meet at angles smaller or greater than a right angle.

items.stem: Which pair of lines is parallel?
items.hint: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never meet.
items.explanation: The lines in C stay the same distance apart, so they are parallel. A and D meet; in B the gap gets smaller, so they would meet if made longer.

items.stem: ABCD is a rectangle. Which side is parallel to side AB?
items.hint: Look for the side that faces AB and never meets it.
items.explanation: DC is opposite AB and stays the same distance from it, so DC is parallel to AB. BC and AD meet AB.

items.stem: Which shape has NO parallel sides?
items.hint: Look for two sides that face each other and stay the same distance apart.
items.explanation: Shape A is a triangle: no two of its sides are parallel. The square, rectangle and hexagon each have pairs of parallel sides.

items.stem: How many books were borrowed on Monday?
items.hint: Follow the top of the bar across to the scale.
items.explanation: The top of the Monday bar is halfway between 40 and 50, so 45 books were borrowed.

items.stem: How many pupils chose red?
items.hint: The scale goes up in 4s. What number is halfway between two lines?
items.explanation: The Red bar ends halfway between 20 and 24. Halfway between 20 and 24 is 22.

items.stem: How many more pupils chose Red than Blue?
items.hint: Read both bars first, then find the difference.
items.explanation: Red is 30 and Blue is 15. 30 − 15 = 15 more pupils.

items.stem: On which day was the number of visitors the least?
items.hint: Look for the shortest bar.
items.explanation: The Wednesday bar is the shortest (15), so the number of visitors was the least on Wednesday.

items.stem: How many fruits are there altogether?
items.hint: Read each bar, then add all three.
items.explanation: Apples 24, pears 16 and mangoes 32. 24 + 16 + 32 = 72 fruits.

items.stem: Which class collected 4 more cans than Class A?
items.hint: Read Class A first, then add 4.
items.explanation: Class A collected 28 cans. 28 + 4 = 32, and Class C collected 32 cans.

items.stem: 40 pupils were asked to choose one sport. How tall should the Badminton bar be?
items.hint: Find the total of the bars that are drawn. How many pupils are left?
items.explanation: Swimming 12 + Football 15 = 27. 40 − 27 = 13, so the Badminton bar should reach 13.

items.stem: The total for Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday is 90. What value should the Wednesday bar show?
items.hint: Read Monday and Tuesday first.
items.explanation: Monday 25 + Tuesday 35 = 60. 90 − 60 = 30, so Wednesday should be 30.

items.stem: Ali’s table says Red 14, Blue 8 and Green 10. Which bar did he draw wrongly?
items.hint: Read each bar and compare it with the table.
items.explanation: The Blue bar reaches 10, but the table says 8. Red (14) and Green (10) match the table.

items.stem: What is 7 × 7?
items.hint: Use the table of 7.

items.stem: What is 63 ÷ 9?
items.hint: Which number times 9 is 63?

items.stem: 8 packs have 6 balloons each. How many balloons are there?
items.hint: Use a multiplication fact.

items.stem: Arrange from smallest to greatest: 1/2, 3/8, 3/4
items.hint: Change all fractions into eighths.

items.stem: Arrange from greatest to smallest: 2/3, 5/12, 1/2
items.hint: Change all fractions into twelfths.

items.stem: Three jugs hold 3/5 ℓ, 1/2 ℓ and 7/10 ℓ of juice. Which jug holds the least?
items.hint: Change all fractions into tenths.

items.stem: The figure is made of two rectangles. What is its area?
items.hint: Split the figure into two rectangles. Find the area of each, then add.
items.explanation: The top rectangle is 4 cm × 3 cm = 12 cm². The bottom rectangle is 5 cm × 2 cm = 10 cm². 12 + 10 = 22 cm².

items.stem: A small square is cut out from one corner of a big square. What is the area of the figure left?
items.hint: Find the area of the big square, then take away the small square.
items.explanation: The big square is 6 cm × 6 cm = 36 cm². The cut-out square is 2 cm × 2 cm = 4 cm². 36 − 4 = 32 cm².

items.stem: Three equal rectangular mats are laid side by side. What area do they cover?
items.hint: Find the area of one mat first.
items.explanation: Each mat is 2 m × 4 m = 8 m². 3 mats cover 3 × 8 = 24 m².

items.stem: What is the perimeter of the figure?
items.hint: Add the lengths of all the sides around the figure.
items.explanation: 7 + 3 + 4 + 2 + 3 + 5 = 24, so the perimeter is 24 cm.

items.stem: Two squares of side 4 cm are joined to make a rectangle. What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.hint: The line in the middle is not part of the perimeter.
items.explanation: The rectangle is 8 cm long and 4 cm wide. 8 + 4 + 8 + 4 = 24 cm.

items.stem: A fence goes around the garden, except for a 2 m gate. How long is the fence?
items.hint: Find the perimeter first, then take away the gate.
items.explanation: The perimeter is 12 + 5 + 12 + 5 = 34 m. Without the 2 m gate, the fence is 34 − 2 = 32 m.

items.stem: A swimming lesson ended at 5.10 p.m. It lasted 50 minutes. When did it start?
items.hint: Count back 50 minutes.

items.stem: A cake must bake for 1 h 15 min and be ready at 3.00 p.m. When should it go into the oven?
items.hint: Count back 1 hour, then 15 minutes.

items.stem: A ferry trip took 2 h 40 min and arrived at 11.10 a.m. When did it leave?
items.hint: Count back the hours, then the minutes.

items.stem: Which number is odd?
items.hint: An odd number ends in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9.
items.explanation: 347 ends in 7, so it is odd. The others end in 6, 8 or 0, so they are even.

items.stem: Which of these numbers is even?
items.hint: Look only at the ones digit.
items.explanation: 518 ends in 8, so it is even. 515, 517 and 521 end in 5, 7 and 1, so they are odd.

items.stem: Ben counts on in twos from 14: 14, 16, 18, 20, … Which is true about the numbers he says?

options.text: They take turns: odd, even, odd, even.

items.hint: Look at the ones digit of each number he says.
items.explanation: Adding 2 to an even number gives another even number, so 14, 16, 18, 20, … are all even.

items.hint: $1 = 100 cents. Change the dollars to cents first, then add the cents.
items.explanation: $3 = 300 cents, and 300 cents + 45 cents = 345 cents.

items.hint: How many cents are in $2? Then add the cents after the dot.
items.explanation: $2 = 200 cents, and 200 cents + 5 cents = 205 cents.

items.stem: A pen costs $1.80. How many cents is that?
items.hint: $1 = 100 cents, and the 80 after the dot is 80 cents.
items.explanation: $1.80 = 100 cents + 80 cents = 180 cents.

items.stem: 275 cents = ?
items.hint: Every 100 cents makes $1. How many whole dollars are in 275 cents?
items.explanation: 275 cents = 200 cents + 75 cents = $2 and 75 cents, written $2.75.

items.stem: 608 cents = ?
items.hint: Take out the whole dollars first. Then write the cents with two digits.
items.explanation: 608 cents = 600 cents + 8 cents = $6 and 8 cents, written $6.08.

items.stem: Mei has 450 cents in her money box. How much is that in dollars and cents?
items.hint: How many groups of 100 cents are in 450 cents?
items.explanation: 450 cents = 400 cents + 50 cents = $4 and 50 cents, written $4.50.

items.stem: What is 3.45 p.m. in 24-hour time?
items.hint: For a time after 12 noon, add 12 to the hour.

items.stem: A train leaves at 21:10. What is this time in 12-hour time?
items.hint: For an hour greater than 12, take away 12 and use p.m.

items.stem: Which of these 24-hour times is in the morning?
items.hint: Morning times are before 12:00.
items.explanation: 08:30 is before 12:00, so it is 8.30 a.m. The other times are after 12 noon.

items.stem: A film starts at 14:20 and ends at 16:05. How long is the film?
items.hint: Count on from 14:20 to 15:20, then to 16:05.
items.explanation: 14:20 to 15:20 is 1 h. 15:20 to 16:05 is 45 min. The film is 1 h 45 min long.

items.stem: A bus leaves at 09:50. The trip takes 35 minutes. When does the bus arrive?
items.hint: First count on to 10:00. How many minutes are left?
items.explanation: 09:50 to 10:00 is 10 min. 35 − 10 = 25 min more, so it arrives at 10:25.

items.stem: A shop opens at 10:00 and closes at 21:30. How long is it open?
items.hint: Count the whole hours from 10:00 to 21:00 first.
items.explanation: 10:00 to 21:00 is 11 h, and 21:00 to 21:30 is 30 min. The shop is open for 11 h 30 min.

items.stem: How much water is in the container?
items.hint: Look at the mark that the top of the water reaches.
items.explanation: The water reaches the 3 ℓ mark, so there are 3 ℓ of water.

items.stem: Read the scale. How much water is in this container?
items.hint: The numbers go up in 2s. What is the short mark between them worth?
items.explanation: The short mark between 6 ℓ and 8 ℓ is 7 ℓ. The water reaches that mark, so there are 7 ℓ.

items.stem: How much more water is needed to fill the container up to the 8 ℓ mark?
items.hint: First read how much water is in it now.
items.explanation: The water is at 5 ℓ. 8 ℓ − 5 ℓ = 3 ℓ more is needed.
